designSummary: Weekly run chart of completed interruptions with a p-chart for context, and a days-between-events chart for self-extubation.
sampleSize: About nine eligible patients a day give about 60 eligible patient-days a week. At a baseline of 38 percent, a weekly p-chart has three-sigma limits about 19 percentage points either side of the centre line, so single weeks show little; the run chart shift rule (six consecutive weeks above the baseline median) will detect a sustained rise to about 55 percent or more within the six months. Self-extubation during interruptions is expected about once every one to two months (0.6 percent of about 40 interruptions a week), so it is plotted as days between events rather than as a weekly rate.
primaryAnalysis: Run chart of the weekly proportion of completed interruptions with the eight-week baseline median, judged by pre-specified shift, trend and runs rules, with countermeasure dates marked.
secondaryAnalysis: Run chart of paired breathing trials; weekly proportion of interruptions with a rescue bolus; days-between-events chart for self-extubation; monthly median ventilator days described.
missingData: Days without a completed tally are counted and reported; charts show the number of eligible patient-days each week; no imputation.
multiplicity: One primary measure; balancing and secondary measures described without testing.
software: Spreadsheet run chart template maintained by the charge nurses with the facilitator.
overfittingGuards: Run chart rules fixed before the A3
Countermeasures introduced one at a time
No subgroup charts beyond the planned breathing-trial chart
summary: About 60 eligible patient-days a week; run chart rules detect a sustained rise; self-extubation on a days-between-events chart.
